title: Analgesia de parto
author: Gabriel Magalhães Nunes Guimarães
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ri6d4he

steps.title: Collect patient variables and consent
steps.instruction: Gather all relevant variables for deciding the anesthetic technique and obtain informed consent.

substeps.instruction: Record patient morbidities, especially tolerance to Valsalva.
Note parity (count only vaginal deliveries).
Obtain subjective assessment of labor viability and expected speed from the obstetric team.
Document the patient’s pain pattern (lumbar, colic, perineal, burning, etc.).
Measure cervical dilation.
Verify availability of required material.
Conduct informed consent: if pain interferes with the process, continue after first relief (7.1); otherwise follow normal consent if the patient allows (7.2).

steps.title: Perform standard epidural analgesia
steps.instruction: Place an epidural catheter, administer the initial analgesic dose and monitor the patient.

substeps.instruction: Orient the patient in the delivery room about the procedure.
After the anesthetic button is pressed, locate the epidural space using loss of resistance to saline.
Advance a multi‑orifice epidural catheter.
Aspirate the catheter several times using varied pressures for more than 5 seconds each attempt.
If aspiration is negative, apply a dressing and return the patient to the lying position.
Monitor the patient with pulse oximetry, PANI and ECG.
Infuse 10 ml of analgesic solution (ropivacaine 0.1 % + fentanyl 5 µg/ml).
Continue monitoring for approximately 30 minutes.
If no hypotension or motor block occurs, declare analgesia, remove monitors and allow the patient to walk or change position.
If motor block or hypotension occurs (rare), treat the hypotension, keep monitoring until analgesia is achieved.
If the initial dose fails, increase ropivacaine concentration to 0.15 % and repeat.
From the second bolus onward, administer 7 ml per epidural dose, maintaining a minimum 30‑minute interval between doses.

steps.title: Perform combined spinal‑epidural analgesia
steps.instruction: Give a subarachnoid dose, then place an epidural catheter and manage subsequent dosing.

substeps.instruction: Orient the patient in the delivery room about the procedure.
After the anesthetic button is pressed, perform a subarachnoid puncture with a 27‑gauge (W27G) needle while the patient is seated.
Inject bupivacaine 2.5 – 5 mg plus either sufentanil 2.5 µg or fentanyl 25 µg into the subarachnoid space.
Keep the patient seated after the spinal injection.
Intensify the anesthetic button, locate the epidural space using loss of resistance to saline, and advance a multi‑orifice catheter.
Aspirate the catheter several times for >5 seconds each attempt; if aspiration is negative, apply a dressing.

Allow the patient to remain seated for at least 5 minutes before lying down (ideal interval between spinal dose and supine position). If lumbar pain remains intense, a partial sacral block may be sacrificed to permit earlier lying.
Monitor with pulse oximetry, PANI and ECG.
Do not infuse any epidural analgesic solution for up to 15 minutes after the spinal dose.
Continue monitoring for approximately 30 minutes.
If no hypotension or motor block occurs, declare analgesia, remove monitors and allow ambulation.
If motor block or hypotension occurs, treat the hypotension and keep monitoring until analgesia is achieved.
If pain persists after 15 minutes, give an epidural bolus of 7 ml of the standard solution (ropivacaine 0.1 % + fentanyl 5 µg/ml).
Maintain a minimum 30‑minute interval between subsequent epidural doses; from the second bolus onward, use 7 ml per dose.
If the initial epidural solution fails, increase ropivacaine concentration to 0.15 %.

steps.title: Perform spinal analgesia (higher dose variant)
steps.instruction: Administer a subarachnoid dose of bupivacaine with opioid and monitor the patient.

substeps.instruction: Orient the patient in the delivery room about the procedure.
After the anesthetic button is pressed, perform a subarachnoid puncture while the patient is seated.
Inject bupivacaine 3.5 – 5 mg plus either sufentanil 2.5 – 5 µg or fentanyl 30 – 40 µg.
Keep the patient seated for 1–2 minutes after the infusion, then have her lie on the bed with the upper body elevated 45 degrees.
Monitor continuously with pulse oximetry, PANI and ECG throughout the procedure.
If no hypotension or motor block occurs, declare analgesia.
If motor block or hypotension occurs, treat the hypotension and continue monitoring until analgesia is achieved.

steps.title: Perform spinal analgesia (lower dose variant)
steps.instruction: Give a subarachnoid dose of bupivacaine with opioid and monitor the patient.

substeps.instruction: Orient the patient in the delivery room about the procedure.
After the anesthetic button is pressed, perform a subarachnoid puncture while the patient is seated.
Inject bupivacaine 2.5 – 3 mg plus either sufentanil 2.5 µg or fentanyl 25 – 30 µg.
Keep the patient seated for 5 minutes after the infusion (or the maximum time she can tolerate).
Monitor continuously with pulse oximetry, PANI and ECG.
If no hypotension or motor block occurs, declare analgesia, then remove monitors and allow walking or repositioning.
If motor block or hypotension occurs, treat the hypotension and continue monitoring until analgesia is achieved.

steps.title: Post‑analgesia care and documentation
steps.instruction: Conclude the anesthesia record, manage the epidural catheter, advise diet, and educate the patient.

substeps.instruction: Close the anesthesia record after analgesia is declared.
If an epidural catheter is in place, keep it until after delivery; it may be useful for perineal analgesia if a laceration occurs.
Determine diet: if there is no increased risk of cesarean section, follow the obstetrician’s usual diet; if risk is slightly elevated, switch to a liquid diet without residues.
Remove all monitors and encourage assisted ambulation.
Instruct the patient on post‑procedure care and warning signs of complications.
